newsitem.title: USA: Spectrum settles, plan seen effective soon.
newsitem.headline: Spectrum settles, plan seen effective soon.

text.p: Spectrum Information Technologies Inc said Monday Judge Frederick Block of the United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York approved the settlement of the securities-related class action commenced against Spectrum in 1993.
As a result, Spectrum expects the effective date of its confirmed plan of reorganization, including the implementation of the class action settlement, to occur on March 31, 1997, it said.

Under the settlement, Spectrum will issue to the class plaintiffs a number of shares of Class A Preferred Stock equal to the number of shares of Spectrum's common stock available under its confirmed plan of reorganization to existing stockholders and the trustee for the company's discontinued Computer Bay subsidiary.

The class plaintiffs will also receive proceeds, net of certain fees and expenses, from $10 million of insurance policies covering Spectrum's prior directors and officers and about $1,350,000 in cash or securities from the defendants and $250,000 from Spectrum.
The plan will provide all general unsecured creditors with 100 percent of the value of their claims plus six percent annual interest on the effective date of the plan.

It also will settle the class action litigation by the payment of $250,000 cash and the delivery of approximately 45 percent of the equity ownership in the reorganized company to a trustee to be distributed to the members of the class. On the effective date, total cash distributions for unsecured claims, administrative claims and priority claims are expected to be approximately $4 million.

Spectrum stockholders will have their holdings diluted but under the terms of the plan current shareholders should obtain the majority of the 45 percent equity ownership in the reorganized company set aside for such shareholders and certain creditors. This should hold true even after the issuance of $300,000 worth of stock to the liquidating trustee of Spectrum's former Computer Bay subsidiary in connection with the settlement of the trustee's multi-million dollar claim against Spectrum, the company said.
The plan also calls for Spectrum's management, employees and non-executive directors participating in developing the plan to receive the remaining 10 percent equity ownership.

Spectrum has 76,675,448 shares of common stock issued and outstanding. On the effective date the shares will be canceled and replaced with one new share of reorganized common stock for each seventy-five shares of existing common stock, resulting in approximately one million shares of common stock issued to existing shareholders. Fractional shares will be rounded off. An equal number of approximately one million new shares of Class A Preferred Stock will be distributed to plaintiffs. Roughly 227,000 new shares of reorganized common stock will be issued pursuant to the incentive stock plan.
